description: Troubleshooting knowledge base for LogSense. Each entry maps an observable log symptom to likely causes and concrete checks. Retrieved by TF-IDF cosine similarity in chatbot.py (see KnowledgeBase.retrieve).

entries.title: Database connection timeout
symptoms: could not connect to database within timeout
connection timed out while acquiring connection
likely_causes: Database server unreachable or restarting
Connection pool exhausted by long-running queries
Network path or security group blocking the database port
Timeout value too low for current query latency
checks: Confirm the database accepts connections from the app host on the configured port
Compare active connections against the server's max_connections limit
Look for slow queries holding pool connections open
Check whether the database restarted around the first failure timestamp

entries.title: Connection pool exhausted
symptoms: TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size reached
unable to acquire connection from pool
likely_causes: Connections leaked by code paths that never close sessions
Traffic spike beyond pool capacity
Slow queries occupying connections longer than expected
Pool size configured too small for worker concurrency
checks: Verify every request path closes or returns its session, including error paths
Compare pool size against total worker and thread count
Identify the longest-running queries during the incident window
Check whether failures correlate with a request-rate increase

entries.title: Upstream HTTP 5xx from a dependency
symptoms: received 503 Service Unavailable from downstream service
likely_causes: Downstream service is unhealthy or deploying
Downstream dependency (its own database or cache) is failing
Request payload triggers an unhandled error in the dependency
Load balancer routing to unready instances
checks: Check the downstream service's own logs and health endpoint for the same window
Confirm whether the failures hit one instance or all of them
Review recent deployments to the downstream service
Verify retry and circuit-breaker settings are not amplifying load

entries.title: Connection refused to a dependency
symptoms: failed to establish a new connection
likely_causes: Target process is not running or not yet listening
Wrong host or port in configuration
Firewall, security group or network policy blocking the port
Service restarted and has not finished binding its port
checks: Confirm the target service is running and listening on the expected port
Compare the configured host and port against the service's actual address
Check whether the target restarted just before the first refusal
Test connectivity from the app host rather than from your workstation

entries.title: DNS resolution failure
likely_causes: Hostname misspelled or environment variable unset
Internal DNS or service discovery outage
Cluster DNS cache or resolver pod unhealthy
Service removed or renamed without updating callers
checks: Resolve the hostname from inside the same network namespace as the app
Confirm the hostname environment variable is set in the running container
Check the DNS service's own health for the incident window
Look for a recent rename or teardown of the target service

entries.title: Read timeout calling an external service
symptoms: socket timeout while waiting for response
likely_causes: Dependency is slow under load rather than fully down
Client timeout shorter than the dependency's normal latency
Large response payload or unpaginated query
Network congestion or packet loss on the path
checks: Compare the client timeout against the dependency's p99 latency
Check whether the dependency reports elevated latency in the same window
Look for an unbounded query or missing pagination in the failing call
Confirm retries use backoff rather than firing immediately

entries.title: Authentication or authorization failure
likely_causes: Credential or API key expired or rotated
Clock skew invalidating signed tokens
Service account missing a required role or scope
Secret not injected into the running environment
checks: Confirm the credential is present and unexpired in the running environment
Check for a recent key or secret rotation
Verify the service account's roles and scopes cover the attempted action
Compare host clock against NTP if tokens are signed and time-bound

entries.title: Out of memory / heap exhaustion
likely_causes: Memory leak accumulating over uptime
Loading an unbounded result set or file into memory
Container memory limit lower than the runtime's heap setting
Traffic spike multiplying per-request memory use
checks: Plot memory use over the process lifetime to separate a leak from a spike
Compare the container memory limit against the configured heap size
Look for queries or file reads without a limit or streaming
Check whether the process was restarted by the OOM killer

entries.title: Disk full or write failure
likely_causes: Log or temp files growing without rotation
Volume undersized for current data growth
Filesystem remounted read-only after an I/O error
Orphaned artifacts or core dumps accumulating
checks: Check free space and inode usage on the affected mount
Identify the largest directories and confirm log rotation is active
Review kernel messages for I/O errors that could force a read-only remount
Confirm temp directories are cleaned between runs

entries.title: Background worker stopped or crashed
likely_causes: Unhandled exception terminating the worker loop
Broker connection lost and never re-established
Worker killed for exceeding a memory or time limit
Deploy or restart that the worker did not recover from
checks: Find the last exception the worker logged before it stopped
Check queue depth to confirm messages are accumulating unconsumed
Verify the broker connection and whether reconnect logic exists
Look for an external kill signal or restart at that timestamp

entries.title: Missing or invalid configuration
likely_causes: Environment variable or secret absent in this deployment
Config file path wrong inside the container image
Schema change shipped without updating the deployed config
Type mismatch, such as a string where a number is expected
checks: Print the resolved config at startup with secrets redacted
Diff the deployed config against a working environment
Confirm the config file exists at the expected path in the image
Check whether the failure began immediately after a deploy

entries.title: Database deadlock or lock timeout
symptoms: could not serialize access due to concurrent update
likely_causes: Transactions acquiring locks in inconsistent order
Long transactions holding locks across external calls
Bulk write competing with interactive traffic
Missing index forcing broad row or table locks
checks: Read the database's deadlock log to see both sides of the conflict
Shorten transactions so they do not span network calls
Standardize the order in which rows and tables are locked
Check for missing indexes on the predicates involved

entries.title: Null or missing field dereference
symptoms: TypeError: cannot read property of undefined
likely_causes: Upstream response shape changed or returned empty
Optional field assumed present without a guard
Partial failure returning an incomplete object
Race condition reading state before it is populated
checks: Read the stack trace to find the exact dereferenced field
Log the upstream payload shape for a failing request
Add a guard or default for the optional field
Check whether an upstream contract changed recently

entries.title: Rate limited or throttled by a provider
likely_causes: Request volume above the plan's quota
Retry storm multiplying load after a transient failure
Missing caching causing repeated identical calls
Quota shared with another service or environment
checks: Compare request volume against the documented quota
Confirm retries use exponential backoff and a cap
Add caching for repeated identical requests
Check whether another environment shares the same API key

entries.title: TLS or certificate validation failure
symptoms: unable to get local issuer certificate
likely_causes: Server certificate expired or was replaced
CA bundle missing or outdated in the container image
Hostname mismatch against the certificate's subject
Intercepting proxy presenting its own certificate
checks: Inspect the server certificate's expiry and subject names
Confirm the CA bundle is present and current in the image
Check whether traffic passes through a proxy that terminates TLS
Verify the hostname used matches a name on the certificate
